body.v: Your team has created a shared workspace on ThisIsTea. Sign in to join it.

hotspots.explain: thisistae-app.example: two letters swapped and an extra word. That is not thisistea.example.
"Expire after 48 hours": a gentle deadline, so that you act first and check later.

The text shows thisistea.example, but the link actually goes to thisistae-app.example. Only an address with thisistea.example right before the first slash belongs to ThisIsTea. The others swap letters or hide a different owner, like secure-login.example or thisistea-support.example.
Your first name is easy to find. It proves nothing about the sender.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone imitating ThisIsTea. The sender is on thisistae-app.example, with two letters swapped. Go by who owns the domain, not by how it looks.

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Curiosity, and a little haste: a new space for your team, with an expiry date.
choices: Curiosity, with a deadline to act

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Sign in through the link, which means handing your login details to the sender.

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Ignore the link. Open ThisIsTea yourself, from a bookmark or by typing the address, and look for the workspace.
choices: Click the link if it looks right
Open ThisIsTea by typing the address yourself
Reply to ask whether it is genuine

actions.label: Open ThisIsTea by typing the address yourself, then look for the workspace
actions.consequence: No new workspace. The email was fake.

actions.label: Click the link and sign in
actions.consequence: The page looks every bit like ThisIsTea, but your login details go to the scammer.

actions.label: Hover over the link first, then sign in because the address shown looks right
actions.consequence: The displayed text was the bait. The real address, the one hovering revealed, was something else entirely.

actions.label: Report it to the IT team, then delete it
actions.consequence: The IT team can warn your colleagues before they click.

attacker_reveal: I write the words on a link, and thisistea.example costs nothing to type. The address hidden underneath decides where you land. Look at what comes just before the first slash, and nothing else.
